THROUGHOUT THESE CONVERSATIONS WE WERE CONSISTENTLY TOLD THAT MEANINGFUL PUBLIC ENGAGEMENT WOULD OCCUR BEFORE ANY REDEVELOPMENT PLANS WERE PUT FORWARD. UNFORTUNATELY, THAT LEVEL OF ENGAGEMENT NEVER MATERIALIZED. NEIGHBORHOOD MEETINGS WERE SCHEDULED AND THEN CANCELED. COMMUNICATION BECAME INCREASINGLY LIMITED, AND MANY INQUIRIES FROM US, THE ARTS COMMUNITY WENT UNANSWERED. THEN LAST WEEK, A PUBLIC MEETING WAS HELD WITH LIMITED NOTICE IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWING THE 4th OF JULY HOLIDAY. MANY CONCERNED NEIGHBORS WERE OUT OF TOWN AND UNAWARE. TWO CONCEPT PLANS PRESENTED NONE OF WHICH INCLUDED AN ART CENTER DESPITE YEARS OF DISCUSSION. MOST IMPORTANTLY, WHEN THE PUBLIC SURVEY AFTER THE MEETING WAS PROVIDED, IT INVITED RESIDENTS TO COMMENT ON THE AMENITIES PROVIDED, NOT WHAT THE COMMUNITY NEEDS AND WHAT PEOPLE WANT. WE BELIEVE THAT THIS PROJECT IS IMPORTANT AND IT DESERVES A BROADER PUBLIC CONVERSATION BEFORE DECISIONS ARE MADE.

INSTEAD OF LITIGATING IT ALL NOW, I WOULD JUST LIKE MR. WASHINGTON TO COME BACK AND JUST BRIEFLY PRESENT TO US NOT MORE THAN FIVE MINUTES ABOUT WHY WE'RE SURE THIS WILL WORK THE NEXT TIME AND THEN MY VOTE WOULD BE YES. IF WE VOTE TODAY, THEN MY VOTE WOULD BE NO. BECAUSE MY CONCERN IS I WANT TO MAKE SURE THAT THE PUBLIC IS PROTECTED NEXT TIME.

segments.speaker: ALAN CLENDENIN
segments.text: COUNCILWOMAN HURTAK.

segments.text: CAN YOU BE MORE SPECIFIC? YOU SAID THERE ARE ALL SORTS OF PROBLEMS.

THEY NEED TO TIME TO RESPOND HERE TO GET DOWN BECAUSE MULTIPLE STORMS TAKING PLACE THAT YEAR BACK IN 2024.
